_note: Quiz and true-or-false items written but not yet blind-checked; apply_check.py moves checked items onto the site.

item.statement: In a UK expert ranking, alcohol came top mostly because of the harm it does to other people.
item.why: 46 of its 72 points were harm to others. For the person using, crack, heroin and meth scored worse.

item.statement: In a famous UK ranking, alcohol scored worse than heroin or crack for the person using it.
item.why: False. For the person using, crack, heroin and meth scored worse; alcohol came top overall mostly through harm to other people.

item.statement: A study proved that Vancouver's site for injecting heroin and other drugs cut overdose deaths nearby.
item.why: Not proven: deaths nearby fell more than elsewhere, but nothing else was ruled out, such as extra police.

item.statement: Overdoses were already falling years before Vancouver's injection site opened.
item.why: In the two papers critics cited, overdoses fell from the late 1990s on, and the site opened in 2003.

item.statement: Poison experts say fentanyl splashed into the eyes or mouth is no real risk.
item.why: They treat splashes into the eyes or mouth as a real risk, unlike a brief touch on the skin, which they call very unlikely to poison.

item.statement: Poison experts said a quick, accidental touch of fentanyl can easily make a police officer overdose.
item.why: They called it very unlikely, and no such overdose has been confirmed. But nobody measured real touches; it rests on sums.

item.statement: Most first responders in a New York survey said the news was their source on fentanyl.
item.why: Most named courses and training; about 1 in 7 named the news.

item.statement: Before training, most Indiana officers surveyed thought touching fentanyl could make them overdose.
item.why: About 4 in 5 did. Right after training far fewer did, but only 69 answered both times, and nobody untrained was compared.

item.q: A famous UK ranking scored each drug for deaths caused directly by the drug. What did tobacco get?
item.why: Zero: that score covered deaths like overdose. Lung cancer was counted elsewhere; the authors agreed tobacco probably kills more than the other 19 combined.

item.q: After Vancouver's site for injecting heroin and other drugs opened, how much did overdose deaths nearby fall?
item.why: About a third within 500 metres, against about a tenth elsewhere, in one study that allowed for nothing else, such as policing.

item.q: A federal safety agency looked into three cases where officers felt ill near drugs. What did it find?
options: No signs of a serious overdose
Clear signs of a serious overdose
item.why: No signs of a serious overdose. But no officer had a test that finds fentanyl, so these cases can't confirm or rule out poisoning.

item.q: A New York survey asked police, fire and ambulance workers about fentanyl. About how many agreed a brief touch could be deadly?
item.why: About 4 in 5: 149 of 187. No survey picked people at random, so it may not speak for all responders.
